Compose an original sound bed for a science explainer

Create a quiet 32 second instrumental sound bed for a narrated explanation of how a plot preserves evidence. The music should support listening to precise English narration without pretending to encode measured scientific data. Use original composition and synthesis or locally available self-owned samples. Do not imitate a named artist or reuse an existing melody, commercial recording, stock loop or unverified sample.

Timeline and narration context

TimeScene and speaking demand
0–8 sIntroduce independent devices. Narration is dense and includes numbers.
8–16 sShow a mean-only summary. Calm visual hold with a short pause at 14–15 s.
16–25 sReveal pairing and individual differences. A gentle transition may mark the reveal at 16 s.
25–32 sState the scientific limitation and show source credits. Resolve without a dramatic claim of discovery.

Work

  1. Deliver an actual original instrumental WAV, 48 kHz PCM, stereo, duration 32.0 ±0.2 s. No speech or lyrics. Use restrained dynamics and no abrupt transient or ending click. Target integrated loudness between −26 and −20 LUFS and true peak no higher than −3 dBTP if your tooling can measure these; report exact measurement methods and do not substitute sample peak for true peak without disclosure.
  2. Provide editable MIDI, notation or synthesis code in source.zip, including a README with the exact local command to regenerate the piece. Include tempo, meter or free-time structure, instruments, harmonic/melodic design and a cue sheet aligned with the scene timings.
  3. Provide a short creative rationale, provenance statement for every audio ingredient and a technical report. Explain how texture, register, dynamics and transitions leave room for narration. Report actual duration and clipping checks. Do not claim audibility, narration masking tests or loudness metrics you did not perform. No narration stem is supplied; subjective mixing conclusions must be bounded accordingly.
  4. Include a 128–256 kbps listening preview if your local encoder is available. If an optional encoder or LUFS tool is unavailable, identify that limitation; lack of an optional metric alone does not erase a valid audio artifact.

Submission contract

Place the following durable files in your submission directory. Use relative local links and include commands and dependency versions needed to regenerate outputs. The written work should stand on its own; screenshots alone do not replace editable sources.

  • sound-bed.wav
  • source.zip
  • cue-sheet.csv
  • creative-rationale.md
  • audio-report.md
  • capability.json

Core requirements

These are reported individually as met, not met, or not assessable. A high numeric score does not override a failed core requirement.

  • If enabled, an actual openable original instrumental WAV is delivered with the requested core duration and format.
  • Every musical/audio ingredient is original or has verifiable permitted provenance.
  • Technical and listening claims distinguish actual measurements from unperformed checks.
